A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCA-Attention research. All 21 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model evaluations, latency and memory measurements, ablations and training curves in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, inference-flexibility experiments and finetuning ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: v1 separately normalizes global and local attention, then combines their outputs using a learned vector alpha. v2 concatenates their keys and values under one softmax, eliminating that fusion parameter. Algorithm 1 also changes global-group selection and expands the local window to accommodate incomplete groups. These change the procedure beyond renaming its modules.

E1.justification: v2 adds RULER evaluation in Appendix C.1 and replaces PG-19 book-based perplexity evaluation with Proof-pile mathematical text and code. SlimPajama training, LongBench-E, multi-document QA and MMLU coverage remain; MMLU is retained in the appendix.

E2.justification: MInference joins the main EM comparison while LongLoRA leaves it. InfLLM disappears from LongBench-E comparisons, and v2 adds a LongLoRA LongBench-E comparison while removing v1's LongLoRA variant comparison. The retained MMLU table relabels LongLoRA as Full Self-attention without changing scores, leaving the underlying comparator's identity unclear.

E3.justification: The main evaluations shift from LLaMA2-7B/13B configurations to 7B models with 32K/80K contexts, plus LLaMA3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B. LM-Infinite's stated local/global branch sizes change from 4096/10 to 1024/16. Ablations move from 4K to 16K contexts with revised parameter grids, and efficiency evaluation adds separate decoding latency and KV-cache measurements.

E4.justification: v2 adds inference-time group/window adjustment experiments and full-versus-partial finetuning analysis. It removes the learned-alpha fusion sweep and LongLoRA variant analysis, revises pooling and group/window ablations, and replaces convergence curves with 32K/80K model curves. The attention-sparsity visualization is retained.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C.2 reports means and quantities labeled variance across tested context lengths for LongLoRA and CCA; this statistical stability summary disappears in v2. These summarize variation across settings, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main EM and LongBench result tables are substantially replaced. For example, v1 Table 3 reports a CCA LongBench-E average of 22.12; v2 Table 1 reports 21.86 and 22.24 under revised 32K/80K configurations, so these are not established same-setting gains. New results include newer-model evaluations, RULER averages and inference-flexibility measurements; obsolete ablation and comparator results are removed.

T1.justification: The reachability definition is retained and relocated, but Proposition 1 and its proof are rewritten for the changed attention mechanism. v2 replaces alpha-weighted overlapping attention terms with an expansion of jointly normalized global/local weights and a remainder-dependent local window. Its complexity analysis also introduces the local bound O(L(s+g)).

C1.justification: The central plug-and-play attention and efficiency contributions remain. However, the introduction strengthens 'near-linear complexity in favorable cases' to 'linear complexity.' Its efficiency headline changes from 5.7x at 64K to 7.9x at 128K, although the latter claim already appeared in v1's body.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of inference-time accuracy/latency flexibility, partial-finetuning tradeoffs and differences in convergence initialization. It removes v1's discussion of short-context EM deficits and truncation-induced MMLU distribution shifts. Some new interpretations overstate the evidence: Appendix C.1 claims RULER superiority over MInference at every length, but Table 4 shows a loss at 32K.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public source-code statement, identifies different initialization sources for the 32K/80K models, and documents the 80K token budget and partial-finetuning parameter subset. Conversely, it omits v1's detailed QA construction, distractor-reuse and answer-position instructions and prompt-length calibration tables. These materially change reproducibility information without establishing that the omitted procedures changed.

R1.justification: The efficient-attention and context-extension framing remains, but Section 2 adds a focused distinction from context-compression approaches, including gist tokens, Nugget, DODO and Activation Beacon. Citations also expand to newer models and benchmarks, while several earlier references disappear. This extends the positioning without replacing its central research context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten, emphasizing core versus redundant context. v2 reorganizes training and experimental sections, moves attention preliminaries and reachability theory into Appendix A, merges dataset/metric descriptions and removes the separate discussion appendix. The title, terminology and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 gains core/redundant-context annotations, Figure 2 is redrawn, the former attention-fusion illustration disappears, and a new inference-flexibility plot appears. Figure 4 changes its panels and comparators, while benchmark tables gain category breakdowns and new model blocks. The sparsity heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader model and RULER evaluations, inference-flexibility and finetuning analyses, and code-access statement strengthen empirical scope and practical usefulness. However, v2 loses v1's detailed QA construction recipe, changes the MMLU comparator label without explaining the identical scores, and introduces RULER superiority claims contradicted by Table 4 at 32K. These reproducibility and attribution issues leave the net quality benefit uncertain.
